THE BLOCK IS THE GRANDI 2019 FINDING — 'Antioxidant defence against environmental stress', a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial of a topical 2% S-acyl glutathione cream, higher minimal erythema dose versus placebo at p = 0.0003.

WHY THIS COMPOSITION AND NOT THE FAMILY'S USUAL ONE. Every other explainer on this store shows an active DESCENDING INTO the skin, and /pages/brightening-glow already carries two glutathione diagrams built that way. Grandi 2019 is not a delivery finding — it measured how much more UV the skin tolerated before it reddened, which is RESILIENCE. So the r1 brief inverted the family composition: the stress arrives from OUTSIDE, from above, and the skin's answer is already in place. Same camera, same eight-layer stack, same warm solution-page palette as the firming pair Malcolm named as the target; opposite direction of interest. That is what keeps this from being a near-copy of a file two clicks away in the same menu.

WHAT r2 CHANGED, ALL OF IT MALCOLM'S, 2026-08-27: 'lets show the peptide molecules/spheres resting on the surface of the skin - and actually creating a protective layer - that the sun rays and the dirt bouce off of. also - the peptide molecules should not have little tails. remove those'. In r1 three spheres floated in the air above the pads. Here a row of clear spheres RESTS ON the quilted surface, shoulder to shoulder in an unbroken line across the full width, and the two daylight shafts strike it and reflect away at the matching opposite angle while the dark angular motes rebound upward.

THE TAILS WERE MINE AND REMOVING THEM FIXED TWO THINGS. r1 briefed a slender acyl tail on each chain because the study active is S-ACYL glutathione, and the tail was meant to tell this molecule apart from the plain three-bead chains already live on the brightening page. Measured across the r1 wave at native pixels, the engines that drew a tail were markedly more likely to draw a FOURTH BEAD — a strand entering the row looks like one. Malcolm disliked them on sight and was right; r2 removed them and the bead count came good almost everywhere.

VERIFIED AT 100% ON THIS FRAME BEFORE PUBLISHING, not from the contact sheet: EXACTLY THREE pearl beads in every sphere along the row, which is the tripeptide and the house depiction the brightening pair established; NO TAIL, whisker or trailing strand on any chain; the covering CONTINUOUS with no gap the motes could fall through; and NOTHING DARK ANYWHERE BELOW IT — the pads, the cream film, the granular band, the fibre zone and the lobules are clean, calm and evenly coloured, with no reddened, blotchy or irritated area in the picture.

THE CLAIMS POINT, RAISED AND OVERRULED, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED. A continuous layer that sun rays bounce off is, visually, a sunscreen mechanic — physical UV reflection is what a mineral SPF does, and this is a cosmetic cream. The r1 brief negated shield, dome, force field and barrier wall by name for exactly that reason. The concern was put to Malcolm in a sentence when he asked for the layer, he was shown a claims-safe alternative alongside it (slot D, where the rays and motes are absorbed and broken apart at the covering rather than reflected), and he chose this one. His store, his call, made with the alternative in front of him.

OTHERWISE THE DISCIPLINES ARE UNCHANGED. Depicted: arrival of stress, interception, and a local response falling off with distance. Not depicted: any before-and-after, comparison, number, percentage (the p-value and the MED belong to the words), measurement or face. Nothing injected — needle, syringe, cannula and filler negated, because this is a topical and an injectable read would be false and regulated. Nothing bleached, lifted or erased, because this block is about defence and not lightening, and the page's own FAQ answers 'is glutathione safe for all skin tones?'. No brand colour: teal is Matrixyl's, clinical blue and copper are the copper-peptide page's, and the only bright thing in frame is the warm white of the light itself.

SQUARE, 1:1, NON-NEGOTIABLE — media-with-text has no aspect-ratio on the media div and the row height is set by the master's own aspect, so a non-square file would make this block taller than f1 and f3. Note the row is also sized by the copy: f2's text column is the tallest of the three, so the square master is cover-cropped a little at top and bottom on the rendered page. That is a layout fact of the section, not a fault in the file.

OPTIMISED, NOT COMPRESSED. Long edge capped at 3000 (the widest the theme's srcset ever requests), EXIF and ICC stripped, quality 95 at 4:4:4. Re-encoding harder was measured on this store on 2026-08-24 and made pages marginally SLOWER: Shopify's CDN transcodes every image to WebP and resizes per srcset, so the source JPEG is never what a visitor downloads, and handing the WebP encoder a picture full of JPEG artefacts costs bits to reproduce them.

NEW FILENAME, NEVER A RE-UPLOAD: Shopify Files suffixes a name collision and keeps serving the original. Checked that this stem is not a prefix of any live file and that no live file is a prefix of it, because the uploader binds by prefix while polling and this repo has twice bound two slots to the same image.
